title: Suarez counters: interior submission also terminates on the image in the one joint act
source_text: LV. Contra vero Franciscus Suarez, quando uno eodemque actu, imago cum exemplari conjunctim adoratur, pertendit non tantum exterius submissionis signum, sed ipsam quoque internam animi submissionem ad imaginem terminari, & submissionem illam non exemplar solum respicere, sed ipsam etiam cum exemplari imaginem: ita ut illius adorationis totius & integrae, objectum sit imago, non vero ejus duntaxat quod in illa adoratione exterius & sensibile est. Dicendum est, inquit, posse recte fieri, ut prototypum in imagine, & imago propter prototypum, uno actu interiori, & exteriori adoretur. Tom. 1. in 3. Tho. disp. 54. Sect. 3. Et ibidem addit; quum aliquis imaginem & prototypum per modum unius objecti apprehendit, hominem ferri ad colendum illud objectum, sicut unico corporis motu, ita etiam unico voluntatis actu: neque oportere in tali actu rationes formales distinguere. Postea vero inde infert, per hanc adorationem, adorari etiam imaginem, non solum actu externo, qui ad adorationem non sufficit, sed etiam interiori motu & intentione adorantis, atque non ita abusive tantum, sed vere ac proprie.
pass_a_gloss: But on the contrary Franciscus Suarez, when by one and the same act the image is adored jointly with the exemplar, maintains that not only the exterior sign of submission, but also the very internal submission of mind, is terminated in the image, and that that submission regards not the exemplar alone, but also the image itself with the exemplar: so that the object of that whole and integral adoration is the image, not merely what in that adoration is exterior and sensible. It is to be said, he says, that it can rightly be done that the prototype in the image, and the image on account of the prototype, be adored by one interior and exterior act. Tom. 1 on ST III, disp. 54, sect. 3. And there he adds; when someone apprehends image and prototype after the manner of one object, the man is carried to cultivating that object, as by one motion of the body, so also by one act of the will: nor is it necessary in such an act to distinguish formal reasons. Afterwards from this he infers that by this adoration the image also is adored, not only by an exterior act, which does not suffice for adoration, but also by the interior motion and intention of the adorant, and not so only abusively, but truly and properly.
pass_b_english: Suarez answers Vasquez: in the joint act, interior submission terminates on the image too—not only the sensible mark.
One interior-and-exterior act adores prototype-in-image and image-for-prototype as one object, truly and properly—not merely abusively.

choices.why: Suarez denies need to split them in the one act.
